top_choice_rationale: P004 (Grossman and Helpman, B013) rewards a compact, mature theory that made protection an equilibrium outcome of lobbying and electoral incentives. It produced sharp, estimable predictions that three decades of empirical work have taken to data. Its credit rests on a stable two-person partnership with jointly authored core papers, which is cleaner than B041, where Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum have uncredited parallel claims. The main discount is the mixed record of the specific Protection for Sale predictions, and I rank it only modestly ahead of P001. P001 (B038, narrow citation, Autor, Dorn and Hanson) is the strongest rival on exactly that axis, with a credible design, more than a decade of scrutiny and converged attribution. P003 follows for its measurement-plus-identification quality, with a discount for maturity and restricted data. P005 follows with attribution concerns. P002 (B001) is canonical and mature but has an indirect link to observed contracts and data and sits in a field with many prior prizes. P000 is last because every slate proposal rests on a valid, substantial contribution.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile. None of my listed co-authors (Kaplan, Axelson, Weisbach, Jenkinson, Lerner, Sørensen, Robinson, Martinsson, Thomann) is credited on any slate proposal. I disclose a long committee overlap with Hassler and Krusell, and Krusell also ranks B013 first; I do not treat that agreement as evidence of merit. I also share an SSE affiliation with Andersson, Dreber Almenberg and Friberg. These are colleague ties, not candidate ties, and none is adjudicated.
